articleTitle: Skin Disease detection based on different Segmentation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The outer integument of the human body is skin. The skin pigmentation of human beings varies from person to person and human skin type can be dry, oily, or combination. Such a variety in the human skin provides a diversified habitat for bacteria and other microorganisms. Melanocytes in the human skin, produces melanin which can absorb harmful ultraviolet radiation from sunlight which can damage the skin and result in skin cancer. The necessary tools needed for early detection of these diseases are still not a reality in most third world communities. If the symptoms of skin diseases such as acne, dermatomyositis, candidiasis, cellulitis, Scleroderma, chicken pox, ringworm, eczema, psoriasis, etc. are left untreated in its early stage then they can result in numerous health complications and even death. Image segmentation is a technique which aids with the detection of these skin diseases. In this paper, image processing techniques like adaptive thresholding, edge detection, K-means clustering and morphology-based image segmentation have been used to identify the skin diseases from the given image set. The acquired image set was pre-processed by deblurring, noise reduction and then processed. Depending on the definite pattern (pertaining to a distinct disease) present in the processed image the disease is detected at the output for a corresponding input image.

articleTitle: A Comparative study of Lung Cancer detection using supervised neural network
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Different data analysis and classification methods have been used for diagnosis and detection of lung carcinoma. Since the cause of lung carcinoma stay incomprehensible, circumvention becomes unattainable, hence early revealing of tumor in lungs is the first way for treatment of lung carcinoma. Therefore, biomedical image processing and machine learning is the process used to classify the presence of lung carcinoma. The motive of this study is to develop precision and determine specific value for detection of lung carcinoma at an earlier stage using a mixture of biomedical image processing technique and knowledge Discovery in Data. The image of the lungs that is obtained from the CT(Computed Tomography) scan images is being pre-processed and the segmentation is being done in the Region Of Interest(ROI), Random Forest method have been applied to classify the distinct features. Saliency Enhancement has been done and using SURF(Speeded Up Robust Features) algorithm features such as entropy, co-relation, energy and variance have been extracted from the Saliency Enhanced images with the help of a SVM (Support Vector Machine) Classifier. Classification identifies whether the image provided is healthy or unhealthy(carcinomic). Minimum objective vs. Number of function evaluation plot is used to study the performance of the method. This entire process has been done using two algorithms - random forest algorithm and SVM classification. The best result is obtained using SVM classification. This procedure is total 94.5% efficient, 74.2% sensitive, 66.3% recall and 77.6% specific.

articleTitle: A Dual Layer Image Encryption using Polymerase Chain Reaction Amplification and DNA Encryption
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Unauthorized access of the data is one of the major threat for the real world digital data communication. Digital images are one of the most vital subset of the digital data. Several important and sensitive information is conveyed through digital images. Hence, digital image security is one of the foremost interest of the researchers. Cryptographic algorithms Biological sequences are often used to encrypt data due to their inherent features. DNA encryption is one of the widely used method used for data security which is based on the properties of the biological sequences. To protect the images from unwanted accesses, a new two stage method is proposed in this work. DNA Encryption and Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) Amplification is used to enhance the security. The proposed method is evaluated using different standard parameters that shows the efficiency of the algorithm.

articleTitle: An application of Li-Fi based Wireless Communication System using Visible Light Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This paper attempts to clarify the concept and applications of Li-Fi technology. The current Wi-Fi network use Radio Frequency waves, but the usage of the available RF spectrum is limited. Therefore a new technology, Li-Fi has come into picture. Li-Fi is a recently developed technology. This paper explains how array of LEDs are used to transmit data in the visible light spectrum. This technology has advantages like security, increased accessible spectrum, low latency efficiency and much higher speed as compared to Wi- Fi. The aim of this research paper is to design a Li-Fi transceiver using Arduino which is able to transmit and receive data in binary format. The software coding is done in Arduino- Uno platform. Successful transmission and reception of data(alphanumeric) has been done.

articleTitle: Segmentation Techniques for Rotten Fruit detection
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Segmentation technique to detect a vegetable quality is a very useful method. An automated system if coupled with such technique would be very helpful in sorting the fresh and the rotten vegetables. The purpose of this research paper is to provide an approach for the segmentation of the rotten vegetables to annihilate infirmity with respect to human health. Segmentation technique such as Marker Based Segmentation, Colour Based Segmentation and Edge Detection, produced promising and effective results. Through the above mentioned segmentation techniques, the rotten portions of a vegetable is detected effectively to separate the unhealthy vegetables from the good ones. Sorting of vegetables for any food product manufacturing unit with the aid of an automated system would reduce time and manpower with greater accuracy. The methods used for detection of rotten vegetables undergo a multi-level analysis. The evaluation for each method was done on eight sets of images (containing healthy and rotten vegetables) and the experimental results validate the potency of the suggested technique.

articleTitle: An Atomic Technique For Removal Of Gaussian Noise From A Noisy Gray Scale Image Using LowPass-Convoluted Gaussian Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: During Acquisition of an image using some digital devices we often observe various types of noises. Between them, one of the major types of noise that we often found is the Gaussian noise. When an image contains Gaussian noise, it produces several impurities which are very difficult to detect and eliminate. As a part of the image restoration process, removal of Gaussian noise from a digital image is always a matter of challenge. Before removal of Gaussian noise, we need to convert the digital image into a grayscale image which may contain different percentages of Gaussian noise. Throughout the last few decades, lots of Gaussian noise removal filters or algorithms have been proposed in different international conference papers and acclaimed journals. But a very few of them were successful as far as detecting and eliminating of Gaussian noise from a digital image is concerned. Moreover, these proposed methods also contain several drawbacks and pitfalls which are creating obstacles regarding the generation of the enhanced output image. In this paper, we propose a unique and atomic technique for removal of Gaussian noise from a digital noisy image which is not only capable of detecting and eliminating Gaussian noise, present in the digital image but also capable of generating an enhanced output image. We also try to establish that our proposed method is giving much better result in comparison to other popular filters or algorithms. In order to do that we have invoked a comparative study in experimental results and analysis portion of these paper by calculating PSNR, MSE and RMSE.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Technique for Computer Vision Based Vehicles License Plate Detection System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Automatic license plate recognition (ALPR) is a process of identification of the license plate from an image taken at any signal stop or parking station. The Identified information or the number plate can be used for keeping a check on signal stops or for monetary settlements at parking lots or toll stations. It can also be used around the world for law and administrative works like checking a vehicle if it is registered or not. It also finds its use in safety supervision system. The ALPR can be used upon various types of pictures like color images, black and white images and etc. ALPR may fail a number of times if the quality of the picture is not up to the mark. So, ALPR depend a lot in the image quality, and hence the challenges in its real-life application. It may be used both indoors and outdoors but it must be able to process the images both quickly and successfully in all sorts of environments, be it daytime or night time, sunny or rainy. Our proposed method mainly has three modules: 1) Detection of license plate 2) Segmentation of Characters 3) Text Box Generation. The number plates sometimes may be unclear for the cameras. It may sometimes have dirt and scratches on it and thus increasing the complexities of the ALPR system. Today nationwide ALPR has been adopted by several law and governmental agencies for its efficiency and usefulness. Public safety agencies are using the ALPR system to gather and store relevant information about people and to keep a check on the vehicular activities. It is becoming a significant tool for the Law Enforcement Agencies.

articleTitle: Advanced ATM System Using Iris Scanner
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Nowadays we are experiencing a radical increase in skimming in the Automated Teller Machine (ATM) systems. So, actuation in advancement and security of the ATM machines is required. An automated teller machine (ATM) is an electronic telecommunications device that helps customers of banking departments in transactions and transfer of money in their accounts. The customer enters their unique personal identification number (PIN), i.e. stored in the chip of the card. Due to an increase in the installation of ATM and the number of ATM cardholders, the number of cases of fraudulence has also increased radically. The advancement in technology has resulted in an increase in various skimming activities. So, developments are incorporated in the existing systems to make it more secure, convenient and reliable. The employed secured system must have high speed and must be durable. The presented design is unique because of biometric scanners such as Iris scanner and the two-way check with fingerprint scanner makes it more reliable. The iris scanner being the primary security check lets the system access the further steps for transaction. Fingerprint scanner embedded in the ATM card acts as the secondary security check for the system. The transaction procedure is successful only if the input data by the card holder matches with the database. It consumes less energy that makes it suitable for use. The suggested modified system is pragmatic moreover economical when correlating to the alternative existing classification and affirmation processes of ATMs.

articleTitle: Sun Tracking Solar Panel Without Microcontroller
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Today we are living in an era where we need to use renewable energy as much as possible because day by day the pollution is increasing. So one of the most usable and efficient renewable energy source is solar panel or solar energy. We have already seen a lot of solar panel systems like static solar panel and sun tracking solar panel. Sun tracking systems are mainly of 2 types, one is single axis solar tracker and dual axis solar tracker. Already many paper has been published on different types of solar panels and already seen the latest one is sun tracking system based on microcontroller. In our project we are trying to make a sun tracking scalable system without microcontroller which can be cheaper than other solar panel circuits in our approach. We hope that this proposal of our system can be efficient in future. This paper proposes a solar system which can track the sun using the reference of two small solar panel and track the path by tracking the difference of two voltages of two reference panels and moves the system structure using stepper motor.

articleTitle: Wireless Voting Machine
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Traditional Voting systems used ballot-paper based voting systems. This system was accompanied by some problems. To curtail some of these problems, two new techniques were used which are biometric finger print recognization and retina scanning. In this paper, the techniques are illustrated in detail and these techniques when implemented in the wireless voting machine as safety measures has proven to be a boon. Thus, wireless voting system has proved to be a advantage in the new age of voting systems.

Author Keywords: wireless voting system proved to be boon

articleTitle: Real-Time Vehicle Detection from Captured Images
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Objective of this paper is to primarily detect moving vehicles from real-time captured images so that we can later use them for a variety of purposes like detecting the number of vehicles that are present at a road at a certain point, understanding the motion of the vehicles, analyzing vehicle density at any traffic signal at any specified point of time; and based on our previous knowledge can make a good assumption where the vehicle will be heading towards. Signal-to-noise ratio, PSNER and mean-square-error are computed for each captured image using after detection. After establishing vehicle detection scheme, we can also make an attempt to read vehicle plate numbers further a much broader attempt to automate a traffic flow system using image recognition and probability distribution.

articleTitle: Masking based Segmentation of Rotten Fruits
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The paper presents a stable machine vision system having certain methodologies which converts images to digital format and execute operations on it for getting an enhanced output though getting required details is the prime concern. Detection by means of segmentation gives a very good result in the output image. A rotten or fresh fruit is detected at the output is a segmentation technique gives an effective result. In this work we have used an algorithm that includes background removal by colour space technique (mainly YCbCr), clustering using L*a*b* colour space and KNN clustering. For an automated system with less time complexity a GUI is designed which can load the image produce the output instantaneously.

articleTitle: Modified Repetitive Controller for Disturbance Rejection of Peristaltic Pump
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of an modified repetitive controller for periodic disturbance rejection of peristaltic pump. An observer based rejection of periodic disturbance is shown here for speed control of peristaltic pump. The input output data samples are taken over finite interval of time with an data acquisition system. Plant model is obtained by using the System Identification Toolbox in MATLAB. Fitness of the model is investigated by applying different dataset in order to achieve the best fit model. Simulation is performed using MATLAB. A comparative study on time domain performance of the system is carried out here to establish the effectiveness of the proposed controller in terms of time domain performances.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation Using Background Subtraction On Colored Images
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This paper on object detection by image processing to ensure the people suffering from various vision disorders to detect and to perceive the real image before them. The image perceived by the patients are rendered and developed so that the closest similar object is detected. The input to the program is a image which is fed to the set of processes which in turn gives a image that can be compared to the set of data to give the accuracy in (percentage) to which extend the image is similar to an object or animal.

articleTitle: Automated Irrigation System Using Arduino and Cloud
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The global population is increasing in an unexpected rate; its direct impact is the pressure on the agricultural sector. In other words, the demand for food is growing day by day, so innovation in the agricultural sector is one of the most important duties of the Engineers today. In this project, an Arduino based Automatic Irrigation System backed up by cloud/server has been developed that serves two major purposes. Firstly, it reduces the manpower needed in the fields as the water supply will be automatic. This also indicates one farmer can now take care of one or more crop, which ultimately leads to an increase in yield. Secondly, with the automation of water supply, crops get the exact amount of water needed considering all the factors like its breed, the season, moisture retentivity and various other factors. We expect an increase in the crop quality with the advent of this technology.

articleTitle: An Automated RFID Based Car Parking System
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this article the authors describe the design of an automated car parking system using RFID technology. For the purpose of identification of radio waves are in form of electronic data transfer between the reader module and tag module which is attached to an object. RFID technology uses RFID tags, RFID readers and RFID antenna. The application can be used for managing and controlling various reports and operations of the parking system. By using this software the check-in and check-out will be in control of the RFID tags, readers and barriers. With this software and technology, the check-in and check-out can be done very quickly by avoiding the traffic jam problem near the gates of parking lots. Drivers will not have to wait for the identification of their vehicles as it will be done automatically by the tags that are provided to them. This will also ensure security as only the registered tags (users) are allowed to enter.

articleTitle: Study of Variation of Q-Factor Using Minimum Power Under Different Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In recent scenario, Free Space Optical (FSO) communication technique plays pivotal role in high data rate cost effective communication system. But the major threat of such transmission technique is atmospheric weather conditions. In this paper, a study is performed on six different weather conditions keeping the Laser source power as minimum as possible to overcome the hindrance of atmospheric turbulence in plain area. The diameters of the transmitting and receiving apertures of the FSO link are varied to obtain superior Q-Factor and height of eye diagram for a particular wavelength of 1550nm using 0.1mW power for a fixed link distance of 500m. For establishing the novelty of this technique six different atmospheric conditions are considered. The simulation of the performance analysis is done using OPTISYSTEM 7.0.

articleTitle: Hybrid Regression Model for Soil Moisture Quantity Prediction
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Predicting quantity of soil moisture would help the farmers who are involved in agriculture. Recently researchers have used various machine learning algorithms to predict the quantity of soil moisture. In this study a hybrid method of different types of regression algorithms have been employed for prediction. The proposed method first clusters the dataset using K-Means Clustering, then for each clusters an individual regression model is trained. The proposed method is compared with other regression models like DT (Decision Tree), MLP (Multilayer Perceptron)-Regressor, LR (Linear Regression), KNN-Regressor and SVM (Support Vector Machine Regression). Experimental results have shown that Hybrid model using Decision Tree Regression achieved an average RMSE of 0.002924 and outperformed other models.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Bandwidth of SIW Cavity-backed Slot Antenna through DR Loading
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In the paper, a low profile SIW based cavity-backed antenna is designed and a narrow rectangular slot is then introduced at its center in the ground plane for radiation purpose. The parent antenna is found radiating at 5.33 GHz with a gain of 4.9 dBi. The antenna depicts narrow bandwidth of 50 MHz. The parent antenna is modified by placing dielectric resonators over the slot to step up the bandwidth. The new antenna produces an impedance bandwidth of 750 MHz which reflects a bandwidth enhancement of 700 MHz. All the antennas are designed by utilizing Arlon AD270 as the substrate material and the results after simulating are juxtapose with that after measurement.

articleTitle: Advanced Air Quality Monitoring System Using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: With an increasing air pollution, we developed an Advanced Air Quality Monitoring System using Raspberry Pi 3B+. The system involves monitoring the air quality by considering parameters like Suspended particulate matter(SPM), Carbon dioxide, Ozone, Carbon monoxide, Smoke, temperature and humidity. Particulate matter being a very important parameter gives a clear indication of pollution in that particular time in the area. These pollutant data are extracted using sensors like MQ7, MQ135, MQ9, DSM501A, DHT11, etc. Most of these sensors produce analog output so an Analog to Digital converter is required before supplying the data to the Raspberry pi 3B+ microcontroller. Using software and coding of the Raspberry Pi 3B+, the data are analyzed and a graph to show the changes in the locality and time in which the experiment is plotted. The results obtained were verified. The experiment is conducted in a locality at Rajarhat, New Town, Kolkata and the results were compared with that from a local environment control authority. This system would help to take real-time decisions and very effective in today's situation of high air pollution in most of the Indian cities.

articleTitle: SIW Based Body Wearable Antenna For IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Antennas are an integral part of wireless communication. With the advances in wireless communication and a wider range of applications utilizing wireless technology, antenna selection and design are more important than ever. The usage of wearable textile materials for developing micro strip antenna segment has risen rapidly. A wearable antenna is a part of the clothing itself and has immense utilization in a wide array of fields such as the Internet of Technology (IoT). In this paper, half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) based semi-circular antennas are presented to operate at IoT frequency band. The HMSIW antenna has been devised at 5.8 GHz of center frequency. The gain comes up to 6.02 dBi. The semi-circular rim of the antenna is indented with metallic vias. This makes it a perfect electrical conductor (PEC) wall. There are no vias on the other side of the semi-circular antenna thus making it a perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) wall.

articleTitle: Implementing Mobile Agent based Secure Load Balancing Scheme for MANET
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Mobile Ad Hoc network consists of short- lived collection of heterogeneous resource constrained nodes. Load balancing can optimally utilize the resources of the nodes, and hence, maximize throughput and network lifetime, while minimizing response time and avoiding overload on any single resource. Consequently, in this paper, we propose a load balancing scheme by exploiting mobile agents.A mobile agent is a program that can migrate from one environment to another autonomously and get executed in the new environment. Agents due to its inherently distributed nature are more suited to MANET as the host (that spawns the agents) need not be connected while the agent is accomplishing its task. Thus, compared to message passing, mobile agents can be better utilized to MANET applications. The proposed scheme is found to be robust against modification attacks on the mobile agents. This scheme is implemented using Aglet platform. The results show the robustness of the scheme.

articleTitle: Study of Optical and Electrical Characteristics of chemically extracted Lotus and Taro Bio-Wax for Hydrophobic Surface Engineering
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This study focuses on the development of a super-hydrophobic layer containing chemically extracted bio-waxes from lotus and taro leaves on silicon (Si) substrates. Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR) have been performed to observe the structural properties and compositional functional groups of the relevant bio-waxes. Contact angle measurement is used to determine the hydrophobicity of the surfaces by measuring respective contact angles at the interface of liquid and bio-wax coated surface. Also, capacitance-voltage (C-V) measurement is performed to determine the dielectric properties of the waxes which indicate possible applications of such bio-derived materials in the domain of digital bio-microfluidics.

articleTitle: Patch Antenna of Self Similar Structure for Wearable Devices Operating Around 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: The applications of wearable medical devices are increasing day by day. They are now becoming an essential part of everyday human life starting from smart watch, smart phone to smart home. The main component of recent technology like the Internet of Things is the wearable devices. Inherently antenna is the essential part for all communicative devices. This paper focuses on antenna design which can be useful for wearable devices. Since they operate in close proximate to the human body, the radiation pattern, frequency of operation and power requirement of the designed antenna must be properly controlled. There are inherently some high frequency hazards of wearable devices which cannot be eliminated and the size of antenna is inversely proportional to frequency. Hence to compensate for these two contradictory requirements fractal designs are introduced, where the antenna can operate at relatively low frequency by essentially increasing the electrical length due to fractal structure. This paper presents the performance analysis or comparison of different iterations of antenna when fractal designs are introduced. The antenna operates around 5.8 GHz, which is a recommended frequency band for wearable devices by Federal Communications Commission (FCC). A high return loss is achieved which in turn indicates a measure of forward power propagation. The antenna is fabricated with FR4 substrate.

articleTitle: A 4 Bit Combinational Hybrid-Junction Splitting Technique for Realization of an Energy Efficient SC SAR ADC
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: A novel technique that combines the advantageous features of hybrid and junction splitting technique is presented for realization of a very high energy efficient SC SAR ADC. The hybrid capacitor switching scheme is very energy efficient in which the first three comparison cycles do not consume any energy. The junction splitting technique involves appending capacitors as each bit is successively being determined by the system. The present paper combines these two features to realize an SC SAR ADC which is more energy efficient than either of the two. The method provides energy savings as well as unit capacitor saving. Thus the method becomes one of the most energy efficient switching schemes among its peers. It achieves a 50% reduction in unit capacitance requirements over the conventional one.

articleTitle: Eradication of Salt and Pepper Noise from a Tumorous MRI image using SNPRB Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Apart from different types of noises which can be represented by categories of modeling style, we have considered a model of addictiveness and salt and pepper type of noise which belongs to impulse category in this outline. We introduce a newly built linear filterization methodology for the eradication of salt and pepper type of noise from a noisy image to achieve restoration over a degradable image. We named our methodology as SNPRB filter which is fundamentally used to deduct above mention noise category from a tumorous image, present inside the human brain and our methodology has produced a positive, desirable and effective result as we observe after experimental result and analysis. In comparison with other pre-existing concepts, our proposed invention generates a far more accurate result as we perform our methodology over multiple data set of some kind and varying noise intensities over our collected data set.

articleTitle: IMC based Fractional-order Controller for a Level Process
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Process modeling and control is one of the most important aspects in any process plant operation with respect to its productivity and product quality. Though proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controllers are widely being exploited in several process industries, however, recently reported control strategies are also being exercised with their respective advantages and suitability for close-loop control applications. Internal model control (IMC) techniques have been widely employed for chemical processes as an acceptable control methodology over prolong period due to their simple structure and hassle free tuning. Recently, the mathematical phenomenon of fractional calculus is being utilized in controller designing. Here, the reported work focuses on designing a fractional order filter based IMC controller for a level control process and its performance evaluation is made in comparison with conventional PID and IMC controllers.

articleTitle: Compact HMSIW Semi-Hexagonal Antennas with Rectangular Slot
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Design of Half-Mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) based compact semi-hexagonal antennas, with the use of a tapered rectangular slot to operate for 5 GHz wireless networks has been discussed in this paper. The parent hexagonal SIW cavity is bisected to obtain half-mode structures which results in two different structures Type-1 resonating at 5.9 GHz and Type-2 resonating at 5.57 GHz. The antennas are subsequently downsized by incorporating narrow rectangular slot having resonance at 4.9 GHz and 4.77 GHz respectively. The design part of the antennas was accomplished using the Arlon AD270 substrate and the simulation deductions are analyzed with the values obtained from measurement.

articleTitle: A nonlinear model-based control scheme for benchmark industrial processes
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Over the last two decades, model-based control schemes have been widely used for designing industrial control systems especially in process control industries. In this paper, a nonlinear model-based control scheme has been proposed for benchmark industrial processes. The scheme also uses adaptive control strategy for better tuning the controller gains. The proposed framework is applied to control the liquid level of a spherical tank, which is a benchmark nonlinear industrial process. Reference tracking and disturbance rejection performance have been tested via simulation results and the performance of the proposed scheme has been compared with the classical adaptive PI controller. Simulation results shows that the proposed scheme ensures closed-loop stability and maintains satisfactory performance in presence of parameter variation.

articleTitle: Measurement of Linear Thermal Expansion Coefficient using Coherent Gradient Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Determination of coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) of metallic bar using coherent gradient sensing (CGS) is reported in this paper. Collimated light interrogated one end of the specimen/sample kept in a furnace. The light which is reflected from the sample is diverted towards the CGS interferometer using the beam splitter (BS). The set-up is arranged such that, the horizontal fringes due to collimation is achieved. Dimensional variation in the specimen is correlated with the size, shape and orientation of the shear fringes. The change in fringe orientation has been used to estimate CTE.

articleTitle: Breast Tumor Segmentation using Image Segmentation Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Breast tumor is one of the major reason of death among women worldwide. The main objective of this paper is to compare the accuracy of three different algorithms used to detect breast tumors. Comprehending the nature of data set in breast images is essential for evolving a model that fits well into the data. The performance of a traditional k-means algorithm is compared with a much more sophisticated saliency map and colour spacing algorithm. The three algorithms have been applied on a breast tumor MRI scanned image, and the results clearly showed the best performance is yielded.

articleTitle: Embedded System based Anti-Flies Knight
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: India is the one of the fastest developing countries in the world in almost every sector. While health still remains one of its top priorities, it has not been able to keep up with the rise in diseases and population burst. Vector borne diseases like dengue, malaria and many more have also been on the rise. People of our country fall short of taking appropriate measures to keep their environment safe. Lack of proper sanitation in remote and inaccessible areas is one of its most important reasons. To tackle this issue, a unique and innovative work has been proposed to ensure the safety of our people against these deadly diseases. A gadget has been devised which will effectively kill and depopulate the vectors and their larvae in a cost friendly and ecofriendly way.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Microstrip Components on Paper Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Feasibility of using “paper” as low cost organic substrate of filter and antenna is studied here. Cutoff frequency for the realized 3-pole low pass filter fabricated on paper substrate (dielectric constant=2.24) is around 2.77GHz having insertion loss less than 0.8dB and minimum attenuation less than -23dB at 7.61GHz (pole frequency). The realized filter has a rejection band from 5.5GHz to 9 GHz with value less than -15dB and achieves at same time acceptable pass band with sharpness factor of 4dB/GHz. A 7-pole low pass filter is also fabricated on same paper substrate. Here rejection band below -20 dB has been found from 2.355 GHz to 15GHz. So rejection bandwidth has been widened from 3.5 GHz to 12.645GHz in comparison with the 3-pole even at -20dB. This filter has sharpness factor of 21.14 dB/GHz which is improved by 17dB compared to 3-pole filter. These sharp low pass filters fabricated on paper substrate have major application in RF receivers.Next a simple circular-polarized antenna is proposed having a square metallic patch with two notches, a ground plane, a probe feed and `paper' as substrate. Experimental result shows that the operating frequency is 2.5GHz with an impedance bandwidth (2:1 VSWR) of 90 MHz and axial ratio less than 0.5db. The simulated cross-polarization isolation obtained is greater than 15dB. The proposed circular-polarized antenna of 2.5 GHz has extensive applications in wireless communication, cellular & satellite communications.

articleTitle: Enhancing the gain of a HMSIW Based Semicircular Antenna using Antenna-FSS Composite Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In the following paper, we have designed a Half Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) based Semi-Circular Patch Antenna to operate at 6.5GHz wireless frequency. The parent antenna is such designed that it has an array of metallic vias along the circumference to make the edges behave as Perfect Electrical Conductor (PEC) walls while the radiation occurs from the radial side which acts as a Perfect Magnetic Conductor (PMC) wall because it is devoid of such metallic vias. The antenna exhibits a gain of 6.2dBi with linear polarization. Its gain is increased using polarization independent Frequency Selective surface (FSS) as superstrate which is fabricated using Arlon AD270 substrate. The gain is found to increase from 6.2dBi to 8.2dBi at the same 6.5 GHz resonating frequency.

articleTitle: Compact Semi-circular Half-mode SIW Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, a semi-circular antenna which is half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) based and fitted with coaxial feed, operating at 5.22 GHz is designed. The same antenna excited with inset feed is also designed to operate at 5.51 GHz. The antenna is reduced in size by including thin rectangular slit(s) on the PMC edge to design two compact antennas working at 4.68 GHz and 3.85 GHz respectively. Using a substrate Arlon 270 the two compact antennas are designed and the measured and simulated results are compared.

articleTitle: Investigating the chemical bath deposited n-SnO2/p-Si heterojunction devices for optoelectronic applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, the SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> thin film is grown on Si-substrate by employing chemical bath deposition (CBD) method. The surface morphology and chemical compositions of such film are obtained from FESEM and EDX studies, respectively. The appropriate concentrations, obtained from EDX study, confirm the formation of SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film with appropriate stoichiometry. The XRD pattern shows poly-crystalline nature of the SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-film with <;310> and <;101>-planes. The optical band gap is measured to be 3.6 eV from the UV-VIS spectrophotometry results. The current-voltage characteristics of such n-SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>/p-Si heterojunction devices under both dark and illuminated condition show significant enhancement of photo current and thereby suggests its potential for using photo detection applications.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide based Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) compact antennas are presented as sensors to operate in the IEEE C-band. The main sensor is a SIW antenna designed at a frequency of 5.8 GHz for IEEE 802.11 WLAN application. The antenna has triangular patch and metallic vias along the edge thereby making it a conductive wall and hence a perfect electrical conductor (PEC) while absence of vias on the other side makes it a perfect magnetic conductive (PMC) wall. The antenna radiates linearly polarized wave corresponding to TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</sub> mode with a corresponding gain of 4.21dBi. The SIW designs are simulated using Arlon AD270 substrate as a dielectric and the simulated results have been obtained.

articleTitle: SIW based Semi-Hexagonal Planar Array Antennas for 5.9 GHz Unlicensed Band
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: In this paper, a 2×2 semi-hexagonal planar array based on half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) has been designed at 5.9 GHz unlicensed band. A gain of 5.8 dBi is exhibited by the single element semi-hexagonal SIW antenna while a gain equal to 11 dBi is produced by the array antenna which reflects gain enhancement by 5.2 dBi. The simulated results obtained by the array antenna, designed using Arlon AD270 substrate are compared with the measured ones.

articleTitle: Computation of Threshold Voltage Shift in Submicron Heterostructure MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Threshold voltage of submicron heterostructure MOSFET is analytically calculated as a function of channel length based on a novel formulated model. Thickness of the dielectric slab, doping concentration of the substrate, and applied horizontal bias are tailored within practical limit to compute the shift of threshold, after validating result for conventional MOSFET. Two-dimensional Poisson's equation is analytically solved for this purpose, and better tuning is observed for nanometric device dimension. Simulated observations have greater for current computation and subthreshold slope evaluation for the hetero-device.

articleTitle: A Wide Band Bandpass Filter Using Floating Split Ring
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Here in this paper a compact wideband bandpass filter (BPF) is presented. The size of the end coupled dual-resonator bandpass filter is reduced with a reasonably wide spacing between resonators. The broadside coupling provided by multi-layered structure is used to produce controllable transmission pole. The first unwanted harmonic is removed by introducing quarter wave resonators. For validation of the design a BPF centred at 2.49 GHz with a 3dB fractional bandwidth of 24% is designed, fabricated and measured. There is good agreement between simulated and measured results. The overall cut out size of the filter is 16x3mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Air Flow Mapping and Profiling using Talbot Interferometry and Fourier Fringe Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: An experimental study is reported for air flow mapping using Talbot interferometry and image processing algorithm. Light from the laser is collimated and are focused on the Talbot interferometer (TI). The set-up is arranged such that the horizontal fringes due to collimation is obtained. When the static pressure probe (for air flow) is inserted between the pair of grating, the change in refractive index between the pair of grating deteriorates the fringe patterns and is used to profile air flow.

articleTitle: Design of High-Performance LED Based Integrating Sphere for Illumination & Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: An integrating sphere has been specially designed using multiple white light LEDs mounted on both the inner and outer surfaces of the sphere to create improved uniform illumination inside a computer laboratory room. The LEDs are simultaneously used as optical transmitters of trans-receiver systems for indoor optical wireless communication. More uniformity of light helps to develop better access to wireless communication systems, comfortable movement inside the room and reduced shadowing effect in wireless communication. One integrating sphere fitted with LED arrays divided among outer and the inner surfaces of the sphere is able to create ideal uniformity conditions for illumination and data communication within a volume (3 × 3 × 3) m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> of laboratory space. The system is capable of bidirectional full-duplex communication using IR LEDs as source for uplink and silicon photodiodes as receivers for optical wireless communication links. The theory and the design principles of the integrating sphere and the optical wireless communication link design would be presented.

articleTitle: The effect of disorder on electronic structure and conducting properties of superconductors with various kinds of pairing symmetries
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: A detailed review of the effect of disorder on superconductivity is done for single band and multiband systems with attractive pairing interactions. We shall go on to investigate the situation where interband interaction is repulsive and intraband interaction is attractive. Such pairing represents a “± s-wave superconductor”. We find that if the form of the intraband pairing potential is nonlocal then superconductivity survives even when the repulsive interband interaction is dominant. Randomness in interband pairing potential is able to kill superconductivity in such a system.

articleTitle: Industrial Internet of Things: A Review
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: For the past few years internet of things (IOT) has become of great interest for both academic and industrial research. The term industrial IOT evolved when IT is integrated with industrial automation and control system. The review in this paper provides with the insights into an overview of industrial internet of things (IIOT), evolution of IOT, transformation of IOT to IIOT, architecture of IIOT, different case studies & IIOT in business. This research study aimed to evaluate up to date position of IIOT in present scenario and providing some research recommendation for future researchers.

articleTitle: Detailed Human Activity Recognition using Wearable Sensor and Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Use of Human activity recognition is increasing day by day for smart home, eldercare, remote health monitoring and surveillance purpose. Serving these purposes better, needs detailed recognition of activities, viz. sitting on chair or floor, slow or brisk walk, running with load, etc. Very few works aim to distinguish between intense activities (such as walk carrying weight) from its counterpart (walk) which is essential for effective health monitoring of elder adults and patients recovering from surgery. In this work, solution has been proposed for this purpose with the help of wearable and smartphone-embedded sensors. Accordingly, the contribution of this work is to present a framework for detailing in identification for both static and dynamic activities, as well as their intense counterparts by designing an ensemble of classifiers. The ensemble is designed that applies weighted majority voting for classification of test instances. Weights of the base classifiers are determined by feeding their output performance for training dataset in a neural network. We observed that our work achieves above 94% recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of Earthworm Optimization Algorithm for solution of Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: Economic and efficient generation of electricity is one of the main concern for power system engineers. To achieve this objective “optimal power flow” or “OPF” problem needs to be solved efficiently in a fast manner. Better quality of electricity is to be produced with required voltage level and reduced cost while satisfying all the system constraints. Modern trend is to apply several population based optimization algorithm in solving “OPF” problem. These optimization algorithms give better results in comparison to the conventional approaches. In this paper a recently evolved soft computing technique namely “Earthworm Optimization Algorithm” (EWA) is used to get the solution of “OPF” of “IEEE 300-bus test system”. Performance of “EWA” in solving “OPF” problems has been evaluated and compared with some of the well-established optimization algorithms. The results obtained using “EWA” seems to be satisfactory in all respect.

articleTitle: Design of Resource/Energy-Efficient Energy Detector for Real-Time Cognitive Radio using WARP
publicationTitle: 2019 International Conference on Opto-Electronics and Applied Optics (Optronix)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of practical realization of real-time Cognitive Radio (CR) enabled opportunistic Secondary Users (SUs) through test-bed design and characterization of energy detection based spectrum sensing using Wireless Open Access Research Platform (WARP). To this end, the SUs leverage the proposed Practical Energy-Efficient Energy Detection (PED) method to sense the incumbent Primary User (PU) channels with high accuracy. The PED method exploits the already existing Carrier Sense (CS) module in a transceiver system for resource efficient implementation of energy detection based sensing. The PED method is further integrated within a proposed Energy Detection based CR Medium Access Control (ECR-MAC) framework developed at the Embedded Processor (EP) for real-time SU operation. The ECR-MAC has been designed to reduce the effective sensing time under medium/high received PU SNR at the SU. Finally, the superiority of PED method, ECR-MAC framework has also been reflected, through performance analysis, in terms of reduced energy consumption in spectrum sensing.
